PLAN "12-Week Fat Loss & Glycaemic Control Plan for Type 2 Diabetes (Integrated Summary)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "fat loss and glycaemic control"

NUTRITION
  calories: moderate deficit (approx. 20% below maintenance)
  protein: 1.6g per kg bodyweight daily
  carbs: 35-40% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables)
  fats: 30-35% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish)
  fiber: minimum 30g daily from vegetables, legumes, whole grains
  meal_frequency: 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks, consistent timing daily
  hydration: minimum 2L water daily
  avoid: added sugars, sugar-sweetened beverages, refined grains (except during cheat meal)
  pre_workout: small balanced meal/snack with protein and low-GI carbs 1-2h before resistance training
  post_workout: protein + moderate low-GI carbs within 1h of resistance training
  fasted_cardio: permitted if morning blood glucose >5.5 mmol/L, otherwise consume small low-GI carb snack before cardio
  cheat_meal: 1 meal per week, preferably lunch, enjoy favorite foods in moderation, avoid sugar-sweetened beverages, monitor portion size, check blood glucose 2h after meal, resume normal plan after
  monitor: blood glucose before and after exercise, adjust carbs if needed to prevent hypoglycaemia

NUTRITION_PREWORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO
  if morning blood glucose >5.5 mmol/L:
    recommendation: "No breakfast required before fasted cardio. Hydrate with water."
  else:
    recommendation: "Consume a small low-GI carb snack 15-30 minutes before cardio, such as:"
    options:
      - "1 small apple or pear"
      - "1 slice whole grain bread"
      - "100g plain Greek yogurt"
      - "1/2 cup cooked oatmeal (unsweetened)"
      - "1 small banana"
    note: "Monitor blood glucose before and after cardio. If feeling lightheaded or blood glucose <4.0 mmol/L, consume 15g fast-acting carbs (e.g. 120ml fruit juice) and stop exercise."

NUTRITION_POSTWORKOUT_SNACKS
  recommendation: "Consume a snack with protein and low-GI carbs within 1 hour after training."
  options:
    - "150g plain Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries"
    - "1 boiled egg + 1 slice whole grain bread"
    - "Protein shake (whey or plant-based) + 1 small apple"
    - "100g cottage cheese + 1/2 cup sliced peach"
    - "1 small can tuna (in water) + 2 oatcakes"
    - "30g mixed nuts + 1 small orange"
    - "Hummus (3 tbsp) + carrot sticks"
    - "Low-fat cheese stick + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes"
  note: "Avoid snacks with added sugars or refined grains. Adjust portion size to fit calorie goals."

NUTRITION_INTERMITTENT_FASTING
  recommendation: "Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered with caution for type 2 diabetes, but only under medical supervision."
  protocol: "If approved by her healthcare provider, a 14:10 or 16:8 fasting:eating window may be used. For example, eating all meals between 10am and 6pm (16:8)."
  considerations:
    - "Monitor blood glucose closely, especially when using metformin."
    - "Do not skip meals after resistance training; always consume a post-workout snack or meal within the eating window."
    - "If feeling lightheaded, weak, or if blood glucose <4.0 mmol/L, break the fast immediately with a low-GI carb snack."
    - "Stay hydrated with water, herbal tea, or black coffee during fasting hours."
    - "Avoid fasting on days with high-intensity or long-duration exercise unless already adapted."
    - "Cheat meal should be within the eating window."
    - "Consult with her doctor before starting IF and adjust medication if needed."
  not_recommended: "IF is not recommended if she has a history of hypoglycaemia, disordered eating, or if her doctor advises against it."

  meal_frequency: 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks, consistent timing daily
  hydration: minimum 2L water daily
  avoid: added sugars, sugar-sweetened beverages, refined grains

  post_workout: protein + moderate low-GI carbs within 1h of resistance training
  fasted_cardio: permitted if morning blood glucose >5.5 mmol/L, otherwise consume small low-GI carb snack before cardio

PLAN "12-Week Fat Loss & Glycaemic Control Plan for Type 2 Diabetes (Integrated Summary)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "fat loss and glycaemic control"

NUTRITION
  calories: moderate deficit (approx. 20% below maintenance)
  protein: 1.6g per kg bodyweight daily
  carbs: 35-40% of total calories, focus on low glycaemic index sources (e.g. oats, quinoa, lentils, beans, sweet potato, non-starchy vegetables)
  fats: 30-35% of total calories, emphasize unsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish)
  fiber: minimum 30g daily from vegetables, legumes, whole grains
  meal_frequency: 3 main meals + 1-2 snacks, consistent timing daily
  hydration: minimum 2L water daily
  avoid: added sugars, sugar-sweetened beverages, refined grains (except during cheat meal)
  pre_workout: small balanced meal/snack with protein and low-GI carbs 1-2h before resistance training
  post_workout: protein + moderate low-GI carbs within 1h of resistance training
  fasted_cardio: permitted if morning blood glucose >5.5 mmol/L, otherwise consume small low-GI carb snack before cardio
  cheat_meal: 1 meal per week, preferably lunch, enjoy favorite foods in moderation, avoid sugar-sweetened beverages, monitor portion size, check blood glucose 2h after meal, resume normal plan after
  monitor: blood glucose before and after exercise, adjust carbs if needed to prevent hypoglycaemia

NUTRITION_PREWORKOUT_FASTED_CARDIO
  if morning blood glucose >5.5 mmol/L:
    recommendation: "No breakfast required before fasted cardio. Hydrate with water."
  else:
    recommendation: "Consume a small low-GI carb snack 15-30 minutes before cardio, such as:"
    options:
      - "1 small apple or pear"
      - "1 slice whole grain bread"
      - "100g plain Greek yogurt"
      - "1/2 cup cooked oatmeal (unsweetened)"
      - "1 small banana"
    note: "Monitor blood glucose before and after cardio. If feeling lightheaded or blood glucose <4.0 mmol/L, consume 15g fast-acting carbs (e.g. 120ml fruit juice) and stop exercise."

NUTRITION_POSTWORKOUT_SNACKS
  recommendation: "Consume a snack with protein and low-GI carbs within 1 hour after training."
  options:
    - "150g plain Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries"
    - "1 boiled egg + 1 slice whole grain bread"
    - "Protein shake (whey or plant-based) + 1 small apple"
    - "100g cottage cheese + 1/2 cup sliced peach"
    - "1 small can tuna (in water) + 2 oatcakes"
    - "30g mixed nuts + 1 small orange"
    - "Hummus (3 tbsp) + carrot sticks"
    - "Low-fat cheese stick + 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes"
  note: "Avoid snacks with added sugars or refined grains. Adjust portion size to fit calorie goals."

NUTRITION_INTERMITTENT_FASTING
  recommendation: "Intermittent fasting (IF) can be considered with caution for type 2 diabetes, but only under medical supervision."
  protocol: "If approved by her healthcare provider, a 14:10 or 16:8 fasting:eating window may be used. For example, eating all meals between 10am and 6pm (16:8)."
  considerations:
    - "Monitor blood glucose closely, especially when using metformin."
    - "Do not skip meals after resistance training; always consume a post-workout snack or meal within the eating window."
    - "If feeling lightheaded, weak, or if blood glucose <4.0 mmol/L, break the fast immediately with a low-GI carb snack."
    - "Stay hydrated with water, herbal tea, or black coffee during fasting hours."
    - "Avoid fasting on days with high-intensity or long-duration exercise unless already adapted."
    - "Cheat meal should be within the eating window."
    - "Consult with her doctor before starting IF and adjust medication if needed."
